fullPassage: In Vallauris, a small town in the South of France, a black limousine was parked outside a barbershop. From inside the car, Pablo Picasso impatiently yelled out. “Please, Arias, hurry up. We’ll be late for dinner.” A curious crowd gathered around the car, wondering who had the nerve to make the legendary artist wait. A few moments later, Eugenio Arias, a man with a cheerful smile, emerged from his modest shop. “Let’s go,” he said as he climbed into the limousine. Despite the fact that Picasso was twenty-eight years older than Arias, the two had been close friends for twenty years. Let’s go back to that summer afternoon when their friendship across generations began. In 1947, Picasso left the crowded city of Paris and moved to the quiet rural town of Vallauris. As a foreigner, he often desperately longed for familiar faces from his home country, Spain. One day, a friend told him about a local barber from Spain named Arias. But for Picasso, it was not easy to visit the barbershop because he had a belief that anyone who possessed his hair or nails would have control over him. Too superstitious to let other people cut his hair, he normally chose to cut his own hair. Eventually, Picasso gathered his courage and entered Arias’s barbershop because he was so eager to meet his fellow countryman. Arias recognized the famous artist right away, but he treated Picasso like an ordinary customer. Leading him to a chair, Arias warmly welcomed Picasso in Spanish. Despite the fact that their conversation was brief that day, Picasso was deeply impressed by Arias’s direct and simple manner of speech. He sensed that Arias was a trustworthy individual with a great sense of humor who put people at ease. Picasso’s visits to Arias’s barbershop became somewhat routine after that. Whenever he visited, the other customers let him be served first. This situation made Picasso feel uncomfortable because it caused other people to wait longer. Sensing his discomfort, Arias asked if Picasso would prefer to get haircuts and shaves at home. Picasso happily accepted the offer. Arias went to Picasso’s house to cut his hair from then on, but he never charged Picasso for his services. In return, Picasso gave him sketches, paintings, and ceramics as a gesture of friendship. As their friendship grew stronger, Arias started to drop by Picasso’s house, not to shave or cut his hair, but to hang out. Picasso once said to Arias, “You are always welcome to come to my house. When you’re here, I feel like I’m back in Spain.” Picasso also paid frequent visits to Arias’s home, where he enjoyed Spanish dishes prepared by Arias’s mother. When they dined together, they would sit and talk for hours. Picasso once asked Arias, “What do you think about your own work as a barber?” Arias answered, “Well, when I finish a haircut for a customer, I always notice my mistakes.” Upon hearing Arias’s response, Picasso suddenly hugged him and said, “You’re an artist. I always see some mistakes whenever I finish my paintings.” One day, Picasso was busy painting War and Peace, one of his largest projects, when Arias paid him a visit. Picasso had been working hard staying up at night for days. Seeing this, Arias assisted Picasso with his work, from moving a ladder around for Picasso to painting some characters. So Picasso made a joke, “Now I have to sign this painting Picasso and Arias.” As time passed, Picasso’s health declined with age. One day, Picasso asked Arias, “What are you going to do with all the paintings and sketches I gave you?” Arias responded that he would build a museum in Spain to display the works. Picasso was moved to hear that and swore to help Arias. But unfortunately, he did not live to see the museum completed, passing away in 1973. Arias was in grief and despair but found comfort in knowing that his best friend would live on through his art. A few years later, Arias returned to Spain and exhibited Picasso’s works. This small exhibit attracted visitors from all over the world. A foreign merchant approached Arias one day and attempted to persuade him to sell all of Picasso’s works. But he refused to bargain, saying, “Even if you bring all the money in your country, I will not sell any of his works to you. His works are symbols of the friendship between Picasso and me.” The Museo Picasso - Colección Eugenio Arias (The Picasso Museum - Eugenio Arias Collection) was finally completed. This was possible because Arias donated approximately sixty pieces of Picasso’s works to Arias’s hometown of Buitrago del Lozoya. They comprised a collection of paintings, posters, ceramics, and other works. Each of them is distinct from Picasso’s other works because Picasso carved each one with the inscription Para mi amigo, Arias (For my friend, Arias). When visitors enter this museum, they quickly discover that it is more than just a tribute to honor Picasso’s artistic legacy; it is also a monument to the artist and barber’s lifelong friendship. The Museo Picasso - Colección Eugenio

피카소는 자신의 머리카락이나 손톱을 가진 사람이 자신을 지배한다고 믿었다.
아리아스는 피카소를 알아보지 못한 채 특별한 손님으로 대했다.

questions.passage: Seeing this, Arias assisted Picasso with his work, from moving a ladder around for Picasso to painting some characters.  So Picasso made a joke, “Now I have to sign this painting Picasso and Arias. ” As time passed, Picasso’s health declined with age.  One day, Picasso asked Arias, “What are you going to do with all the paintings and sketches I gave you? ” Arias responded that he would build a museum in Spain to display the works.  Picasso was moved to hear that and swore to help Arias.  But unfortunately, he did not live to see the museum completed, passing away in 1973.  Arias was in grief and despair but found comfort in knowing that his best friend would live on through his art.  A few years later, Arias returned to Spain and exhibited Picasso’s works.  This small exhibit attracted visitors from all over the world.  A foreign merchant approached Arias one day and attempted to persuade him to sell all of Picasso’s works.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ② 아리아스가 작품을 전시할 미술관을 스페인에 짓겠다고 함 (일치)
det.analysis:
❌ ① 작업을 전혀 돕지 않고 지켜보기만 함: 본문은 아리아스가 사다리를 옮기고 인물을 칠하며 '도왔다(assisted)'고 했으므로 틀리다

✅ ② 미술관을 스페인에 짓겠다고 함: 'he would build a museum in Spain to display the works'와 일치한다 ← 정답

❌ ③ 미술관 완공을 직접 본 뒤 세상을 떠남: 본문은 그가 '미술관이 완성되는 것을 보지 못하고(did not live to see the museum completed)' 1973년에 떠났다고 했으므로 틀리다

❌ ④ 외국 상인에게 작품을 전부 팖: 본문은 그가 '흥정을 거부했다(refused to bargain)'고 했으므로 틀리다
det.tip: would build a museum in Spain = 미술관을 짓겠다

ch: 아리아스는 피카소의 작업을 전혀 돕지 않고 지켜보기만 했다.
아리아스는 피카소의 작품을 전시할 미술관을 스페인에 짓겠다고 했다.
피카소는 미술관이 완공되는 것을 직접 본 뒤 세상을 떠났다.
아리아스는 외국 상인에게 피카소의 작품을 전부 팔았다.

questions.passage: ” One day, Picasso was busy painting War and Peace, one of his largest projects, when Arias paid him a visit.  Picasso had been ①<u>working</u> hard staying up at night for days.  ②<u>Seeing</u> this, Arias assisted Picasso with his work, from ③<u>moving</u> a ladder around for Picasso to painting some characters.  So Picasso made a joke, “Now I have ④<u>to signing</u> this painting Picasso and Arias.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ to signing → to sign (have to + 동사원형)
det.analysis:
✅ ① working: 'had been working hard'는 과거완료진행형(계속 작업해 왔다)으로 알맞다

✅ ② Seeing: '이것을 보고(Seeing this)'는 동시상황을 나타내는 분사구문으로 알맞다

✅ ③ moving: 'from moving a ladder'는 전치사 from의 목적어로 온 동명사로 알맞다

❌ ④ to signing → to sign: 'have to'는 '~해야 한다'는 뜻으로 뒤에 동사원형이 오므로 'to sign'이 되어야 한다. to signing은 틀리다 ← 정답
det.tip: have to + 동사원형(sign)

questions.passage: Eventually, Picasso gathered his courage and entered Arias’s barbershop because he was so eager to meet his fellow countryman.  Arias recognized the famous artist right away, but he treated Picasso like an ordinary customer.  Leading him to a chair, Arias warmly welcomed Picasso in Spanish.  Despite the fact that their conversation was brief that day, Picasso was deeply impressed by Arias’s direct and simple manner of speech.  He sensed that Arias was a trustworthy individual with a great sense of humor who put people at ease.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 피카소가 아리아스를 '믿을 만한 사람'이라고 느꼈음을 나타내는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 2단어로 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: trustworthy individual (믿을 만한 사람)
det.analysis: 본문 'He sensed that Arias was a trustworthy individual with a great sense of humor'에서, 피카소는 아리아스를 '믿을 만한 사람(trustworthy individual)'이라고 느꼈다. 형용사 trustworthy가 명사 individual을 꾸미는 2단어 표현이다.
det.tip: trustworthy(믿을 만한) + individual(사람)

questions.passage: One day, Picasso asked Arias, “What are you going to do with all the paintings and sketches I gave you? ” Arias responded that he would build a museum in Spain to display the works.  Picasso was moved to hear that and swore to help Arias.  But unfortunately, he did not live to see the museum completed, passing away in 1973. questions.stem: 위 글에서 아리아스가 슬픔과 절망 속에서도 위안을 찾을 수 있었던 근거로, 그가 알고 있던 사실을 본문에서 찾아 9단어로 (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: his best friend would live on through his art
det.analysis: 본문 'found comfort in knowing that his best friend would live on through his art'에서, 아리아스는 '가장 친한 친구가 그의 예술을 통해 계속 살아 있으리라는 것'을 알았기에 위안을 얻었다. knowing that 뒤 that절의 내용을 9단어로 그대로 옮긴다.
det.tip: knowing that + [his best friend ~ his art]

questions.wa: his best friend would live on through his art
accept: his best friend would live on through his art

questions.passage: Upon hearing Arias's response, Picasso suddenly hugged him and said, "You're an __________ (art). I always see some mistakes whenever I finish my paintings."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥과 어법에 맞게 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.korean: artist (명사, 예술가)
det.analysis: art(예술) → artist(예술가): 'You're an ___'에서 관사 an 다음, be동사의 보어 자리이므로 사람을 나타내는 명사가 와야 한다. 피카소가 아리아스에게 '너는 예술가다'라고 말한 문맥이므로 art를 사람 명사 artist로 바꾼다.
det.tip: an + ___ 보어 자리 → 사람 명사 artist

questions.passage: In Vallauris, a small town in the South of France, a black limousine was parked outside a barbershop.  From inside the car, Pablo Picasso impatiently yelled out.  “Please, Arias, hurry up.  We’ll be late for dinner. ” A curious crowd gathered around the car, wondering who had the nerve to make the legendary artist wait.  A few moments later, Eugenio Arias, a man with a cheerful smile, emerged from his modest shop.  “Let’s go,” he said as he climbed into the limousine.  Despite the fact that Picasso was twenty-eight years older than Arias, the two had been close friends for twenty years.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① 피카소와 이발사 아리아스가 세대를 뛰어넘어 맺은 평생의 우정
det.analysis:
✅ ① 세대를 뛰어넘은 평생의 우정: 글 전체가 스물여덟 살 차이를 넘어 20년간 이어진 피카소와 이발사의 우정을 다루므로 주제로 알맞다 ← 정답

❌ ② 피카소의 예술적 업적: 그림 이야기는 우정을 보여 주는 소재일 뿐 글의 초점이 아니다

❌ ③ 이발사 직업의 영감: 지엽적 내용으로 전체를 대표하지 못한다

❌ ④ 스페인 이민자의 문화적 어려움: 본문에서 다루지 않은 내용이다
det.tip: friendship across generations = 세대를 뛰어넘은 우정

questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ 나이와 신분을 초월한 진심 어린 우정은 값을 매길 수 없다
det.analysis:
❌ ① 실수를 인정하는 데서 예술이 나온다: 일부 대화 소재일 뿐 글 전체의 요지는 아니다

❌ ② 유명 인사는 특별 대우를 당연히 여긴다: 오히려 피카소는 특별 대우를 불편해했으므로 반대다

✅ ③ 나이·신분을 초월한 진심 어린 우정은 값을 매길 수 없다: 아무리 큰돈을 줘도 작품을 팔지 않고 '우정의 상징'이라 한 결말이 이를 뒷받침하므로 요지로 알맞다 ← 정답

❌ ④ 작품 가치는 시장 가격으로 결정된다: 돈으로 환산하기를 거부한 본문과 정반대다
det.tip: 값을 매길 수 없는 우정 — 작품을 팔지 않은 결말이 근거

ch: 진정한 예술은 완벽함이 아니라 실수를 인정하는 데서 나온다.
유명 인사는 특별한 대우를 받는 것을 당연하게 여긴다.
나이와 신분을 초월한 진심 어린 우정은 값을 매길 수 없다.
예술 작품의 가치는 결국 시장 가격으로 결정된다.

questions.passage: ” Picasso also paid frequent visits to Arias’s home, where he enjoyed Spanish dishes prepared by Arias’s mother.  When they dined together, __________.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 [조건]에 맞게 빈칸을 (영어로) 쓰시오.

함께 식사할 때면, 그들은 몇 시간 동안 앉아서 이야기를 나누곤 했다.

[조건] (1) and, for, hours, sit, talk, they, would 를 모두 사용할 것 (2) 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: they would sit and talk for hours (7단어)
det.analysis: '함께 식사할 때면 그들은 몇 시간이고 앉아서 이야기하곤 했다'는 과거의 습관을 would로 나타낸다. 'they would sit and talk for hours'에서 would 뒤에 동사원형 sit과 talk가 접속사 and로 병렬 연결되고, 'for hours'는 '몇 시간 동안'을 뜻한다.
det.tip: would(과거의 습관) + sit and talk(병렬) + for hours

questions.wa: they would sit and talk for hours
accept: they would sit and talk for hours
